title: Integration profile
description: One service's facts for the integrations module: where it authorizes, where its API lives, how to learn who connected, and its quirks. A profile is data only. Bundled profiles live in kirak/integrations/profiles/; a project adds its own as integrations/<name>.json.

profile_version.description: The version of this format. Only 1 exists.

name.description: The profile's name, used as kirak.json "profile" and as the file name.

docs_url.description: The vendor documentation the facts were checked against.

auth.description: How the app authenticates: the type, the endpoints, and where the token sits in the response.

type.description: oauth2 for a user's own account; api_key for one app key or one key per user.

authorize_url.description: The authorize endpoint. May hold {settings.x}, {connect.x} or {connection.x}.

token_url.description: The token endpoint. May hold placeholders, and a {connection.x} value from the callback or the connect call (Zoho's data center); when that value is the whole host, its pattern must list the allowed hosts.

refresh_url.description: The refresh endpoint. Defaults to token_url.

revoke_url.description: The revoke endpoint, when the service has one. Alone, it means the RFC 7009 request: POST a form with token and token_type_hint, the client authenticated as token_auth says. May hold {client_id} in its path (GitHub).

revoke.description: How a service that does not follow RFC 7009 revokes a token at disconnect. Every field is optional; the defaults are the RFC 7009 request. The token is never put in the URL.

client_auth.description: How the client id and secret go: HTTP Basic, in the body, or not at all. Default: as token_auth.

credential.description: bearer: the token itself authorizes the call, in Authorization: Bearer (Dropbox, Slack). Then the body does not carry it.

format.description: How the body is sent: form (default), json, or no body (with credential bearer).

token_param.description: The body field that holds the token. Default token.

token.description: Which token to revoke. Default: the refresh token when the connection has one, else the access token.

authorize_params.description: Extra query parameters on the authorize URL, such as access_type or prompt.

grants.description: The grants the service supports for this profile: authorization_code (a user connects; the default) and client_credentials (an app-level token, no user). An instance chooses one with grant in kirak.json.

token_params.description: Extra fields on the code exchange (the token request at connect), such as Shopify's expiring. They cannot replace the grant's own fields.

refresh_params.description: Extra fields on the refresh request. They cannot replace the grant's own fields.

pkce.description: Use S256 PKCE. Set it when the service documents it; without a value the default is true.

token_auth.description: How the client proves itself at the token endpoint: basic (default) or body send the client id and secret; private_key_jwt sends a JWT signed with the app's private key (KIRAK_INTEGRATION_<NAME>_PRIVATE_KEY), as auth.jwt describes.

jwt.description: For token_auth private_key_jwt: the JWT the client signs. Sent as client_assertion (RFC 7523) by default, or as the client_secret itself (Apple). Claim and header values may hold {client_id}, {token_url} (the token endpoint being called) and {settings.x}.

as.description: client_assertion (default): sent with client_assertion_type jwt-bearer, signed per request with a jti. client_secret: sent as the client_secret, reused until near its expiry (Apple).

algorithm.description: The signing algorithm; the private key must fit it (EC for ES*, RSA for RS* and PS*).

lifetime.description: Seconds the JWT is valid. Default 300; Apple allows up to six months.

claims.description: The claims, as templates. Default for client_assertion: iss and sub {client_id}, aud {token_url}. iat and exp are added, and jti for client_assertion.

header.description: Extra JWT header fields, as templates, such as kid: {settings.key_id}.

check.description: How `kirak integrations check` proves the client credentials: code (default) sends a code that cannot be valid, for a service that checks the client before the code; client_credentials sends a client_credentials grant; none means no request proves them (the check reports unverified).

token_format.description: How the token request body is sent. Default form.

token_path.description: Where the access token sits in the token response, dotted, e.g. authed_user.access_token. Default access_token.

refresh_token_path.description: Where the refresh token sits in the token response, dotted from the top. Default: refresh_token next to the access token.

expires_in_path.description: Where the access token's lifetime in seconds sits in the token response, dotted from the top. Default: expires_in next to the access token.

expires_at_path.description: Where the access token's expiry as a Unix epoch sits in the token response, dotted from the top, for a service that sends a time instead of a lifetime. Used when no lifetime is found.

scope_path.description: Where the granted scopes sit in the token response, dotted from the top. Default: scope next to the access token.

refresh_expires_in_path.description: Where the refresh token's lifetime in seconds sits in the token response, dotted from the top (QuickBooks: x_refresh_token_expires_in). Default: refresh_token_expires_in next to the access token.

refresh_token_lifetime_days.description: How long a refresh token lasts when the response does not say, counted from each response that returns one (Xero: 60). Without it and without the response field, the expiry is not known.

scope_param.description: The authorize parameter that carries the scopes: a name such as "scope" (default) or "user_scope", or false when scopes are set at app registration (Notion).

scope_separator.description: What separates scopes in the scope parameter. Default a space.

refresh_rotates.description: The service issues a new refresh token on every refresh; the old one must be replaced at once.

expiry_lookup.description: When the token response has no expires_in, where to read the expiry: a URL (may hold placeholders) and a dotted JSON path. The value is seconds from now.

path.description: Dotted path to the expiry value in that response, in seconds from now.

key.description: Where the credential goes: the key (api_key), or the access token (oauth2; default Authorization with the prefix 'Bearer ', Shopify: X-Shopify-Access-Token with no prefix).

in.description: Where the key goes: a header, the query string, or HTTP Basic with the key as the user name (BambooHR, Freshdesk).

name.description: The header or query parameter name that carries the key. Required for header and query.

prefix.description: Text put in front of the key, such as Bearer with a trailing space (header only).

password.description: basic only: the fixed password sent with the key, such as X. Default empty.

scopes.description: The scopes the profile asks for by default, the scope that grants a refresh token, and what each known scope means.

default.description: Scopes requested when kirak.json does not set scope.

offline.description: A scope that makes the service return a refresh token; always added when the service needs it.

known.description: What each known scope means, keyed by scope name.

satisfied_by.description: For the granted-scope check: a requested scope counts as granted when one of these scopes is, because the service grants it under another name (Google: email as https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email) or a wider scope implies it (Shopify: write_products implies read_products).

settings.description: Values the app sets in kirak.json under the instance's "settings" key, such as a tenant or a shop. Each must have a pattern when a placeholder uses it.

default.description: The value used when kirak.json does not set it.

pattern.description: A regular expression the value must match in full. Required when a placeholder uses the setting.

connect.description: Values the app passes to the connect call, such as the shop of a Shopify store. Each has a pattern.

pattern.description: A regular expression the value must match in full.

description.description: What the app passes to the connect call.

sites.description: For a token that reaches several sites, organisations or tenants (Atlassian sites, Xero organisations): the request that lists them. Every site is saved with the connection, the default (else the first) is active, and the app can make another active later; connection values with from site are read from the active one.

url.description: The URL that lists the sites, called with the new access token.

body.description: A JSON body sent with POST. Fixed text: no placeholders are filled in it.

items_path.description: Dotted path to the list in the response. Default: the response is the list.

id.description: Dotted path in a site's item to its id.

label.description: The site's name shown to users: a dotted path in its item, or a template of paths in braces.

default.description: Dotted path in a site's item to a field that is true for the default site. Without it, or when no site has it, the first is the default.

connection.description: Values saved with the connection and used in its URLs, taken from the token, the callback, the connect call or a request.

from.description: Where the value comes from: the token, the callback, the connect call, a request, or the connection's active site (path read in the site's item; the profile needs a sites section).

path.description: Dotted path in the source to read the value from. A step may pick a list item by a field: accounts[is_default=true].base_uri.

key.description: Name of the query parameter or field to read the value from.

method.description: For from request: the HTTP method. Default GET.

body.description: For from request: a JSON body sent with POST, such as a GraphQL query. Fixed text: no placeholders are filled in it.

pattern.description: A regular expression the value must match in full.

method.description: A body is sent with POST only.

account.description: How to learn who connected: the account id and a label to show.

from.description: Where the account id comes from: the id token, the token response, the connection, or a request.

url.description: For from request: the endpoint to read the account from.

method.description: For from request: the HTTP method, POST for a service whose endpoints take POST only (Dropbox). Default GET.

id.description: Dotted path to the account id in that source.

label.description: A label for the account shown to users: a dotted path (email), or a template of dotted paths in braces ({first_name} {last_name}). A missing value is left out; an empty label is none.

body.description: For from request: a JSON body sent with POST, such as a GraphQL query ({"query": "{ viewer { id email } }"}). Fixed text: no placeholders are filled in it.

method.description: A body is sent with POST only.

api.description: Where the service's API lives and what every request carries.

allowed_hosts.description: Extra hosts the API may call, besides the host of base_url. Entries may use a *. wildcard for subdomains.

default_headers.description: Headers every request carries, such as an API version.

errors.description: How the service reports a failure, when its HTTP status does not say enough.

code_path.description: Where the service's error name is in the body, as a dotted path. Default: error.

success_path.description: For a service that answers 200 for errors: a body field that is true on success, as a dotted path. Anything else is a failure.

errors_path.description: For a service that answers 200 with a list of errors (GraphQL: errors): a body field that is a non-empty list on failure, as a dotted path.

token_invalid.description: Error names that mean the token is no longer good: the call refreshes once, then the user must connect again.

scope_missing.description: Error names that mean the grant lacks a scope: no refresh; the connection check reports it.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for one request.

pagination.description: How list responses are paged, so a client can read every page.

style.description: How the next page is found: a Link header, a cursor, a next URL, an offset, or a page number.

param.description: The query parameter that asks for the next page (cursor and page styles). When paginate() is given a body, the body field instead.

next.description: The response field that holds the next cursor or URL.

size_param.description: The query parameter that sets the page size.

max_size.description: The largest page size the service allows.

items_path.description: Dotted path to the list of items in the response body.

offset_param.description: The query parameter that sets the offset (offset style).

total.description: The response field that holds the total count, when the service reports one.

more.description: A response field that is true while more pages follow (Dropbox and Notion: has_more). When set, paging stops once it is not true, even if a cursor came back.

continue_path.description: Cursor style with a body: the path the following pages are posted to, with only the cursor in the body (Dropbox's /files/list_folder/continue). Without it, the next page goes to the same path with the cursor added to the first body (Notion).

rate_limit.description: How the service reports limits: the statuses that mean limited, and the headers that say when to retry.

status.description: HTTP statuses that mean the app is limited.

retry_after.description: Response header that says how long to wait before retrying.

remaining.description: Response header with the calls left in the window.

limit.description: Response header with the call limit of the window.

used_limit.description: Response header with the calls used and the limit in one value, used/limit (Shopify's X-Shopify-Shop-Api-Call-Limit: 32/40). The calls left are the limit less the used. For a service that sends no remaining and limit headers.

reset.description: Response header with when the window resets: seconds, a duration (6m0s, 120ms), an HTTP date or an ISO 8601 time.

reset_epoch.description: Response header with the reset time as a Unix epoch.

limits.description: Several limits reported at once, each with its own headers (OpenAI: requests and tokens). A call is held or refused when any of them is spent. Instead of the section's own remaining / limit / used_limit / reset / reset_epoch.

name.description: The limit's name, as client.quota and the logs show it: requests, tokens, day.

remaining.description: Response header with the calls left in the window.

limit.description: Response header with the call limit of the window.

used_limit.description: Response header with the calls used and the limit in one value, used/limit (Shopify's X-Shopify-Shop-Api-Call-Limit: 32/40). The calls left are the limit less the used. For a service that sends no remaining and limit headers.

reset.description: Response header with when the window resets: seconds, a duration (6m0s, 120ms), an HTTP date or an ISO 8601 time.

reset_epoch.description: Response header with the reset time as a Unix epoch.

scope.description: Whether the limit applies per connection or per integration.

verify.description: One cheap request that proves the connection or key works.

method.description: HTTP method of the verify request.

path.description: Path of the verify request, relative to the API base URL.

body.description: A JSON body sent with POST, such as a GraphQL query. Fixed text: no placeholders are filled in it.

method.description: A body is sent with POST only.

limits.description: Caps the service sets on an app.

max_connections.description: Connections the app may hold for this service, across all users.

webhooks.description: How the service signs and labels its webhooks: the signature scheme, the event name, the delivery id, the handshake, and where the account id is in the payload.

secret.description: Which secret checks the signature: the instance's webhook_secret, or its client_secret.

signature.description: The signature: a header, HMAC-SHA256 of a signed string, hex or base64, with an optional prefix. Or, with kind token, a header that carries the shared secret itself.

kind.description: hmac (default): an HMAC of the signed string. token: the header holds the shared secret itself (GitLab's X-Gitlab-Token), compared in constant time; weaker, since the value does not depend on the body, so kirak validate warns. A token scheme takes only header and prefix.

header.description: The header that carries the signature.

secret_encoding.description: text (default): the secret's text is the HMAC key. base64: the secret encodes the key (Standard Webhooks, used by Svix).

secret_prefix.description: With a base64 secret: text before the base64 that is not part of the key, such as whsec_. Removed when present.

encoding.description: How the digest is written. Default hex.

prefix.description: Text before the digest in the header, such as sha256=.

signed.description: The string that is signed: {body}, {timestamp}, {method}, {url} and {header.<name>} (a request header, such as Standard Webhooks' {header.webhook-id}). Default {body}.

parts.description: For a signature header made of comma-separated key=value parts (Stripe and Calendly: t=1700000000,v1=<hex>): the key of the digest, and of the timestamp when the header carries it. Every part with the signature key is tried, so a header listing two (a secret being rotated) passes when either matches.

signature.description: The key of the digest part, such as v1.

timestamp.description: The key of the timestamp part, such as t. Then timestamp needs no header.

separator.description: What separates the parts. Default a comma; Standard Webhooks uses a space (v1,<sig> v1,<sig>).

delimiter.description: What separates a part's key from its value. Default =; Standard Webhooks uses a comma.

timestamp.description: The timestamp, with the window (in seconds) a delivery may be out by: in its own header, or in the signature header (parts.timestamp).

header.description: The header that carries the timestamp. Needed unless parts.timestamp names it.

handshake.description: A request the service makes to check the URL. Kinds query and body are answered before the signature is checked; kind hmac only after it.

kind.description: query: a query parameter is echoed back as text. body: a JSON body field is echoed back as JSON (Slack's challenge). hmac: a signed delivery that matches gets back a body value and its HMAC with the webhook secret (Zoom's endpoint.url_validation).

param.description: For kind query: the query parameter.

match.description: For kinds body and hmac: body fields and the values that mark a handshake, such as {"type": "url_verification"}. For hmac the keys may be dotted.

answer.description: For kind body: the field to echo back.

value.description: For kind hmac: dotted path to the value to sign, such as payload.plainToken.

echo.description: For kind hmac: the answer field that holds the value, such as plainToken.

hmac.description: For kind hmac: the answer field that holds the value's HMAC, such as encryptedToken.

algorithm.description: For kind hmac: the HMAC's hash. Default hmac-sha256.

encoding.description: For kind hmac: how the HMAC is written. Default hex.

event.description: The event's name: a header, or a field of the body (Zoom's event, Stripe's type), and optionally a field of the body for the action (issues.opened). Exactly one of header and path.

header.description: The header that names the event.

path.description: Dotted path in the body to the event's name, for a service that sends no event header.

action_path.description: Dotted path in the body to the action, appended to the event name.

delivery_id.description: Where the delivery's id is, used to drop duplicates: a header, or a field of the body. Exactly one of the two. Without it, the body's hash is the id.

header.description: The header with the delivery id.

path.description: Dotted path in the body to the delivery id (Typeform's event_id).

account_path.description: Dotted path in the body to the account id the event belongs to.

notes.description: Plain-language quirks, for people and agents.

examples.description: Example calls for people and agents, shown by the catalog.

title.description: A short name for the example.

path.description: Path relative to the API base URL.

endpoint.description: An https URL, or one that starts with a {settings.x}, {connect.x} or {connection.x} placeholder whose pattern holds the value to https. A placeholder may appear anywhere in it.
